walkthroughs.body_html:
Reproduction & Fertility — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Reproduction & Fertility brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Reproduction & Fertility.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why is a reflex action faster than a conscious response?
options: The signal does not need to be processed by the brain — it travels through a simpler reflex arc via the spinal cord.
The brain decides reflexes faster than other actions because it skips thinking.
Reflexes are faster because they use specially fast neurones not used elsewhere.
Active transport only happens in animals and facilitated diffusion only in plants.

mcqs.q: What distinguishes active transport from facilitated diffusion?
options: PCR uses enzymes from bacteria to cut DNA into fragments, then sticks them back together.
Both move substances down a concentration gradient, but active transport is faster.
Active transport requires energy (ATP) and can move substances against the concentration gradient.
Active transport only happens in animals and facilitated diffusion only in plants.

mcqs.q: What are the three repeated stages of one PCR cycle?
options: PCR has just one stage — heating the DNA until it copies itself.

mcqs.q: Which type of cell division produces gametes (sex cells) with half the chromosome number?

mcqs.q: At fertilisation a sperm (23 chromosomes) fuses with an egg (23 chromosomes). How many chromosomes does the resulting zygote have?
Why do offspring produced by sexual reproduction show variation, while those from asexual reproduction do not?
options: Sexual reproduction mixes alleles from two parents.
Asexual reproduction always involves mutations.
Sexual reproduction produces identical clones.
Asexual reproduction uses two parents.

mcqs.q: FSH is given as a fertility drug to some women. What is its main effect?
options: It stimulates eggs to mature in the ovaries.
It prevents eggs from being released.
It thickens the cervix to block sperm.
It lowers blood glucose levels.
